classes.name: GLP-1-based anti-obesity medications
classes.description: Injectable or oral GLP-1/GIP agents labeled for chronic weight management (NOT their diabetes-labeled versions): semaglutide (Wegovy, including Wegovy tablets), tirzepatide (Zepbound), liraglutide (Saxenda). Many plans exclude weight-loss drugs entirely; an exclusion is a valid finding (outcome nonformulary).
classes.plainDescription: A weekly shot (or daily pill) for weight loss, like Wegovy or Zepbound.

classes.name: Oral anti-obesity medications
classes.description: Oral anti-obesity agents: phentermine (Adipex-P, Lomaira), phentermine/topiramate ER (Qsymia), naltrexone/bupropion ER (Contrave), orlistat (Xenical). Many plans exclude weight-loss drugs; an exclusion is a valid finding (outcome nonformulary).
classes.plainDescription: A pill for weight loss, like phentermine or Contrave.

preferredAgent.sig: 2.4 mg by subcutaneous injection once weekly after dose titration (standard label dosing)

criteria: Treatment is for management of obesity; patient is 12 or older (liraglutide labeled minimum)
Adults: BMI >30 kg/m², OR BMI >27 kg/m² with a weight-related comorbidity; under 18: BMI ≥95th percentile for age and sex
Prescriber attests participation in complementary nutritional and lifestyle changes
Not used with other FDA-approved obesity medications, DPP-4 inhibitors, or other GLP-1 receptor agonists; no personal or family history of MTC or MEN2
Trial and failure of two preferred agents; AND clinically valid reason why brand Saxenda cannot be used

records.verificationNote: No Wegovy, Zepbound, or Saxenda line appears in the text. The ANTI-OBESITY/ANOREXIANTS heading on p.11 lists no products. The document does not state the list is exhaustive. Diabetes-labeled Ozempic, Mounjaro, Trulicity, and Rybelsus are listed on p.30 but are not weight products and are not used here. Scope p.3: the Essential Formulary applies to the listed Small Group plans (Bronze/Silver/Gold/Platinum) and Individual Marketplace plans (Bronze 07-20, Silver 26-35, Gold 08). Page numbers are PDF page indexes (PDF page 11 = printed page 1). The document has no statement that the list is exhaustive. [Sonnet check 2026-10-21: Corrected earlier note (the ANTI-OBESITY wording is a shared heading, not an empty section). Absent from the full text and index (pp.98-120): Wegovy, Zepbound, Saxenda, phentermine, Adipex-P, Lomaira, benzphetamine, diethylpropion, phendimetrazine, Qsymia, Contrave, orlistat (naltrexone alone is listed on p.33, not Contrave). The p.11 heading "ADHD/ANTI-NARCOLEPSY/ANTI-OBESITY/ANOREXIANTS" is one shared category whose only subsections are AMPHETAMINES, ANALEPTICS, ADHD AGENTS and STIMULANTS - MISC.; it has no separate weight-loss entries. No weight-loss exclusion wording found; p.5 says only "Certain medications may not be covered if subject to legislative and/or regulatory requirements." Unlisted is not recorded as excluded; confirm with plan. Diabetes GLP-1s (Ozempic pen/tablets, Rybelsus, Mounjaro, Trulicity, p.30) are PA diabetes products and are not weight-loss coverage.]
